subject: MSA redlines: liability cap, OSS pass-through & model licensing

Subject: MSA redlines: liability cap, OSS pass-through & model licensing

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for taking our MSA draft. Attached are our proposed redlines (Bluebird_MSA_redlines_20260310.docx) and a short CSV listing open-source dependencies discovered during our legal review (bluebird_oss-deps_20260310.csv).

Two areas we need to resolve quickly:
- Liability cap / carve-outs: We need a drop-through for third-party claims related to OSS used in the service (pass-through indemnity to allow us to protect our customers).
- Model licensing & training data: we require explicit warranties that the models and any hosted model components do not violate upstream model licenses or third-party data rights; where OSS is implicated we expect the vendor indemnity to flow to us.

We’re trying to close procurement this month. Can you confirm Redwood’s ability to accept a limited pass-through for OSS claims and whether you’d accept an exclusion to the consequential damages carve-out for IP infringement claims?

Thanks,
Elena Vasquez
Head of Legal Ops
Bluebird Labs

Elena —

Thanks for the redlines and the OSS dependency list. I’ve looped in Laura from Legal and Rishi for commercial context. Quick summary of what we need from our side before we can accept/run with your proposed language:

1) A brief note from Bluebird confirming the list of OSS components is complete (or that you’ll notify us of material changes).
2) Clarify the scope of the "pass-through" you want (direct claims from OSS licensors vs. customer-facing regressions/bug claims).
3) Any required cap number you have in mind for pass-through exposure.

Laura — can you review the attached redlines and propose our internal position on the OSS pass-through and the consequential damages carve-out? We’d like to propose options to Bluebird instead of an all-or-nothing counter.

Next step: if legal alignment is possible this week, I can set up a short sync with Bluebird to go live on redlines.

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, Elena Vasquez <elena.vasquez@bluebirdlabs.com>

Subject: RE: MSA redlines: liability cap, OSS pass-through & model licensing

Priyom / Elena —

I reviewed Bluebird’s redlines and the OSS dependency list. High-level recommended positions for Redwood (positions are intentional alternatives to present in a call):

1) Liability cap: propose a commercial cap equal to the greater of (i) the fees paid to Redwood in the 12 months prior to the claim or (ii) USD 1,000,000. This is a common middle ground; we can offer USD 2,000,000 for enterprise-tier deals if needed, but we should reserve that for exec sign-off.

2) Carve-outs: Redwood will accept standard carve-outs for gross negligence and will not accept a broad carve-out for consequential damages to swallow IP indemnities. Specifically: we are willing to keep consequential damages excluded generally, but IP infringement claims and documented regulatory fines arising from Redwood’s breach should be outside that exclusion (i.e., recoverable).

3) OSS pass-through indemnity: we cannot accept unlimited passthrough for all downstream claims tied to OSS. Risk reasons:
   - We do not control upstream maintainers or future license assertions; unlimited passthrough could create unpredictable exposure.
   - Some OSS licenses (e.g., certain copyleft behaviors) have ambiguous remedies in commercial contexts.

Counterproposal (recommended):
   - Redwood will accept a limited pass-through indemnity for direct claims by an OSS licensor asserting removal or copyright/license infringement tied to an included OSS component, capped at USD 250,000 per claim and USD 500,000 aggregate.
   - Pass-through applies only where (a) the OSS was included by Redwood (not customer-supplied code), (b) Redwood fails to remediate within a reasonable cure period, and (c) Bluebird provides prompt notice and cooperation.

4) Model licensing & provenance: we will add representations that the model variants provided have been evaluated against their license terms to the best of Redwood’s knowledge and that we will provide a list of third-party model artifacts and their licenses upon request. However, we cannot warrant absolute non-infringement for models trained on mixed/third-party data. For higher-risk use cases we recommend a third-party IP review clause and a mechanism for expedited removal of a model variant if a valid claim arises.

5) Operational controls: suggest adding an OSS notice-and-takedown process, an SLO for remediation, and an obligation to maintain an updated OSS dependency manifest in the Drive link.

If acceptable to Bluebird, we can draft tracked changes for the above positions. If Bluebird requires higher caps or unlimited pass-through, we’ll need executive approval and insurance confirmation.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: proposed tracked changes (I will upload a marked-up MSA after alignment)

Subject: Re: MSA redlines: liability cap, OSS pass-through & model licensing

Thanks, Laura — that’s helpful and produces a pragmatic starting point. A few quick responses from Bluebird:

• The pass-through we’re requesting is specific to claims by third-party OSS licensors (copyright/license infringement) that directly impact our ability to distribute a combined product to our customers. We are not asking for unlimited consequential damages for other downstream commercial claims.

• Regarding the cap, USD 250k per claim / 500k aggregate is lower than what our procurement requires. Our security and procurement teams would be comfortable with USD 1M aggregate for OSS pass-through but we could accept lower per-claim buckets if remediation timelines are tightened and we get the notice-and-takedown flow-down to our customers.

• On model warranties: Bluebird cannot accept language that places absolute warranty on model provenance. We’d be open to a middle ground where Redwood provides license manifests, commits to best-efforts provenance checks, and carries a carve-out that allows Bluebird to pass downstream limited claims if Redwood’s negligence is proven.

Can we schedule a 30-minute call Friday to walk through open items? Jordan from our outside counsel will join as well.

—Elena
Head of Legal Ops, Bluebird Labs
